snippet.title: Six People Killed In Poland… Within 48 Hours, Officials Were Discussing More Gun Restrictions
snippet.description:
Poland already has some of the strictest firearm licensing requirements in Europe.

Police permits. Medical and psychological evaluations. Firearm registration. A legally accepted reason to own a gun.

Yet on November 7, 2026, a gunman opened fire in Kraków's historic city center, killing six people and injuring 15 others.

And here's what makes this story particularly important.

**THE SHOOTER LEGALLY OWNED FIREARMS.**

According to Polish prosecutors, he had obtained firearm permits earlier in the year.

Within days of the attack, government officials were already discussing whether licensed gun owners should be allowed to possess so many firearms, including different types of weapons kept at home.

In this video, Colion Noir examines Poland's existing gun laws, the government's response to the Kraków shooting, and what happens when a country already has many of the restrictions frequently proposed in America's gun control debates.

We also discuss Poland's firearm registration requirements, access to semi-automatic rifles, and the distinction between preventing violent attacks and responding to them after they occur.

The Polish government has called for a review of its regulations, but additional restrictions have not yet been enacted.

**If a country already requires extensive gun licensing and screening, what additional measures would meaningfully prevent another attack?**

snippet.title: Abdul El-Sayed: "I worry that we may not earn our mandate"
snippet.description:
Abdul El-Sayed is one of the breakout figures of the newly elected Democratic Congress. Voters in Michigan elected the epidemiologist and former public health official to serve in the U.S. Senate and he will be the first Muslim to serve in the upper chamber. Winning that election was far from easy. Republicans, including President Trump, unleashed bigoted vitriol against him and there were plenty of naysayers within the Democratic party who believed his policies were too radical to win in the swing state.

Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed sat down with NPR host Leila Fadel to talk about whether old-guard Democrats and newcomers are ready to unite and tackle the frustrations that propelled the party’s sweeping victories.

You can watch El-Sayed’s interview, where he talks about Democratic party leadership and how he plans to work alongside lawmakers who spewed some of the sharpest vitriol, in the full video.

Do dziś żałuję, że ta historia potoczyła się w tak niesprawiedliwy sposób 😢 Bo jako dzieci odbieramy takie sytuacje jeszcze mocniej i to one nas kształtują. A nie ukrywam - to bardzo namieszało mi w głowie! 🫣

Czy obraz, który wzbudził w nas smutek powinien zająć I miejsce, a ten który nas rozbawił do łez II? 🤷 ...bo w sztuce nie chodzi tylko o idealne pociągnięcia pędzla, idealną technikę. Chodzi o coś więcej, o coś, czego naprawdę nie da się obiektywnie ocenić.

snippet.title: Loki travels to the future of the TVA and witnesses destruction #fyp
snippet.description:
*"If I don't make it back, I—"*
*"You'll make it back."*
*"He'll make it back."* ⏱️

Two men reassuring a god. The god is about to stand inside the heart of the TVA and **prune himself on purpose**, because the only way to stop slipping through time is to tear himself out of it.

*"Am I ready to get my skin peeled off? I don't know. Am I ready to rip myself from every thread of time?"* — *"There has to be another way."*

There isn't. **Ouroboros** — O.B. to his friends — has already done the math: *"We're having power surges all through the TVA. The branching is overloading the Temporal Loom."*

*"The Temporal Loom is the heart of the TVA. And it's not constructed to weave together so many new branches — so it's overloading."*

The fix is ugly. Close the blast doors to save the building, and leave one man outside with a timer synced to the Loom: *"You'll stand by to prune yourself within moments after this turns green."*

And no do-overs: *"Once those doors close, we won't be able to re-sync you, so — it's now or never."* 💀

Because Loki has already been yanked through the TVA's own past and into its future, and what he saw there wasn't a building. It was an ending.

*"It's the future."* — *"Sylvie, I was in the future and I saw you. The TVA is in danger. And you were there. I need to know why."*

So he goes to find her — and finds her behind a counter, in an apron, in a world that doesn't know her name. 🍔

*"Bill, order's up."* — *"Thanks, Sylvie."*

That's the reveal. The woman who killed the man at the end of time, who cracked the entire multiverse open, is working a fast-food shift and being thanked by a guy named Bill.

*"It's a short break, so talk fast."*

*"So you see the future now? Cool."* 😐

She doesn't want it. She has a life — small, ordinary, real — and no interest in being dragged back into anybody's cosmic argument.

*"Explain what I saw, then."* — *"I don't know. I don't care. It's the future. It's going to happen."* — *"Is it?"*

So he asks her for the one thing she can actually give: *"Enchant me. You can see what I saw."* — *"I don't want to see."*

Because she already knows what's in there. She lived it.

*"This is bigger than the TVA. This is about everything."* — and her answer is a question that cuts deeper than any threat: *"You like it here? You've made a home?"*

Yes. She did. And that's the whole fight — he's begging her to help him save the bureaucracy she spent her entire life running from, and she's telling him the thing he's defending is *"the problem. It's broken."*

*"Those are people. Those are lives. Some defense."*

And his reply is the line that redefines him: *"If what He Who Remains said is true, the TVA is the only defense. And if what I saw of you is true, then there's nothing that stands between this world and utter destruction. Without the TVA, all of this, everything… is gone."*

The god who once wanted a throne is now the last man in the room arguing that the institution which ruined his life is worth saving. 🕰️

And she says the plainest, hardest thing in the season:

*"I'm going home… if it's still there."*
*"Please, don't."*
*"It's harder… to stay."*

Not "to leave." **To stay.** Because for someone who has only ever survived, choosing to be ordinary is the scariest thing there is.

And while they stand there arguing in a fast-food lobby, the Loom is still overloading, the blast doors are still counting down, and Mobius is still out there waiting on a timer that has to turn green.

💬 If you could see the future and nobody would believe you — what would you do? And was Sylvie right to walk away from all of it?

🎬 A scene from **Loki, Season 2, Episode 1 "Ouroboros"** (Disney+, 2023).
